notes: CONFORMS (2026-11-16, kb/Work PB5886 and PB5891): §1989:A.2.2 AR4 "An arithmetic expression which will always result in an integer value must be specified" (cite.py OK). The rule sets no method of proof. The classifier FAILS CLOSED at --std 85 as at every edition (IntegerViolation's expression arm, NotAlwaysIntegral) and decides EXACTLY: it builds the argument's value as a polynomial in its atoms (Build: a fixed-point item is 10^-scale times an integer atom keyed by its place; an integer-type function by the type its definition gives, an index-name, a counter register are integer atoms; a numeric function and a floating-point item are real atoms that must cancel; a function whose value its arguments do not fix, RANDOM, is never one atom with another; a quotient by a nonzero literal is the product by its reciprocal, by anything else refused), shows every intermediate exact (Intermediate) and admits the argument when the polynomial is integer-valued on the grid of its degrees (Polynomial.FractionDigits, cap degree 12 per atom). So FACTORIAL (N * (N + 1) / 2), MOD (N * (N + 1) / 2, 4), CHAR (N * (N - 1) / 2 + 65), RANDOM (N * (N + 1) / 2), FACTORIAL (N * (N + 1) * (N + 2) / 6) and MOD (SQRT (N) - SQRT (N) + 5, 7) compile and give 720, 2, C, a value below 1, 3628800 and 5 at N = 3 (pb5891_polynomial_integer_arguments). Refused with COBOL1627: FACTORIAL (FUNCTION ORD (A) / 2), FACTORIAL (FUNCTION MOD (N 3) * 0.5), FACTORIAL (FUNCTION INTEGER (N) / FUNCTION INTEGER (M)), MOD (I / I + 65, 7), MOD (1024 ** K, 7) (witnesses pb5886-*), FACTORIAL (N * (N + 1) / 3), MOD (RANDOM - RANDOM + 1, 7), MOD ((N ** 13 - N) / 13, 7) past the cap and FACTORIAL (T (1) - T (2) + 1) over a scaled table (witnesses pb5891-*), with the earlier refusals pb5208-*, pb5832-*; FACTORIAL (S2 - FUNCTION MAX (S2)) over a scaled S2 stays refused, MAX (S2) and S2 being two atoms equal only by MAX's meaning (the residue of kb/Work PB5889). The admitted shapes are pinned by pb5886_integer_term_shapes, pb5832_scaled_integral_shapes, pb5345_power_failopen_shapes and the shape table of IntrinsicTypeSixPowerShapesDriftTests. 1985 has no EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION, so this screen is the rule's whole enforcement. The ALL subscript half holds (ORD-MAX and ORD-MIN over TC (ALL, ALL), TC (ALL, 2), an ODO range; witness 1989-AR-A_2_2-4). retired-witness: conformance:cases/15.3-Arguments/pb5889-identity-difference (kb/Work PB5891: the type 6 classifier decides by a polynomial normal form; CollectAdditive is deleted, NotAlwaysIntegral moved to IntrinsicArgumentRules.TypeSix.cs, and pb5889-identity-difference's program (SQRT (N) - SQRT (N) + 5) is now admitted, carried by pb5891_polynomial_integer_arguments) retired-witness: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs#CollectAdditive (kb/Work PB5891: the type 6 classifier decides by a polynomial normal form; CollectAdditive is deleted, NotAlwaysIntegral moved to IntrinsicArgumentRules.TypeSix.cs, and pb5889-identity-difference's program (SQRT (N) - SQRT (N) + 5) is now admitted, carried by pb5891_polynomial_integer_arguments) retired-witness: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/Binding/IntrinsicArgumentRules.cs#NotAlwaysIntegral (kb/Work PB5891: the type 6 classifier decides by a polynomial normal form; CollectAdditive is deleted, NotAlwaysIntegral moved to IntrinsicArgumentRules.TypeSix.cs, and pb5889-identity-difference's program (SQRT (N) - SQRT (N) + 5) is now admitted, carried by pb5891_polynomial_integer_arguments)

next.reason: §1989:A.2.2 AR4, as amended in place by X3.23b-1993: out-of-range arguments - 'then the result of such a reference is undefined' (printed: 'the returned value for the function is undefined'), and an ALL subscript yielding no argument - 'otherwise the result of the reference to the function-identifier is undefined' (printed: 'otherwise the returned value is undefined'). The amendment changed what is undefined (the reference, not only the returned value); it changed no accepted program. §2023:15.3 AR14 keeps the ALL-subscript expansion word for word, including 'otherwise the result of the reference to the function-identifier is undefined', and §2023:8.4.2.3.4 GR1 restates it ('If ALL is specified, the subscript is all of the possible values of a subscript for the associated table'). But for out-of-range arguments 2023 replaces 'undefined' with 'the EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exception condition is set to exist' and, when checking is not enabled, 'the implementor defines the result of the function reference': undefined made an exception condition and implementor-defined. 2023 also adds a case: 'If the subscript ALL is specified for a dynamic-capacity table, the range of values of the subscript is from 1 to the current capacity of the table'. The integer argument type is unchanged in substance: §2023:15.3 AR6 'An arithmetic expression that will always result in an integer value or an integer data item shall be specified' against 1989 'An arithmetic expression which will always result in an integer value must be specified' (an integer data item is such an expression).
